definition_en: a farm or place where milk is produced, a shop selling milk, or products made from milk
core_image: 清晨，奶牛排队走进挤奶棚，桶里冒着热气
scene: 清晨，奶牛排队走进挤奶棚，桶里冒着热气。The dairy sends fresh milk to the town each morning.
sceneCN: 这里 dairy 指「奶牛场」（第 1 个义项：生产牛奶的地方）；句意是这个奶牛场每天早上把鲜奶送到镇上。

senses.title: A milk farm
senses.definition: a farm or building where milk is produced and kept
senses.definitionCN: 生产并存放牛奶的农场或房屋
senses.example: The dairy sends fresh milk to the town each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这个奶牛场每天早上把鲜奶送到镇上。
senses.why: Milk must be collected in one place before it can travel.
senses.whyCN: 奶总要先在一个地方聚起来，才能往外送。

senses.title: A milk shop
senses.definition: a shop that sells milk, butter, and cheese
senses.definitionCN: 出售牛奶、黄油和奶酪的店铺
senses.example: He bought butter at the dairy.
senses.exampleCN: 他在乳品店买了黄油。
senses.why: Before fridges, milk had to be sold the same day it came.
senses.whyCN: 在没有冰箱的年代，奶得当天就卖掉。

senses.title: Made from milk
senses.definition: relating to milk or made from it, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 与奶有关或用奶制成，用在名词前
senses.example: The dairy counter was full of cheese.
senses.exampleCN: 乳品柜台摆满了奶酪。
senses.why: A place word can turn into a label for what it sells.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方的名字，能变成它卖的东西的标签。

intro.en: Dairy comes from Old English dæge, a woman servant, whose duties grew to include milking and making milk products.
intro.cn: dairy 源自古英语 dæge（女仆），她的活计逐渐包含挤奶和做奶制品。

items.en: Dæge named a woman servant in a household.
items.cn: dæge 指家里的女仆。

items.en: Her work came to include milking the cows.
items.cn: 她的活儿后来包括给奶牛挤奶。

items.en: Dey became the place where milk was worked.
items.cn: dey 变成处理牛奶的地方。

items.en: Dairy named both the room and the farm for milk.
items.cn: dairy 既指做奶的屋子，也指产奶的农场。

items.en: Dairy now also covers milk products and their industry.
items.cn: dairy 如今还涵盖乳制品及其行业。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dai- shape, and the meaning group names milk and the places that handle it.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dai- 外形，近义组列出牛奶与处理牛奶的场所。

entries.definition: a small white flower with a yellow centre
a place where milk is turned into butter
entries.definitionCN: 把牛奶做成黄油的场所

entries.definition: the white liquid produced by cows
the act of taking milk from an animal
entries.definitionCN: 从动物身上取奶的动作

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with cows walking into a shed and end with a counter full of cheese.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从奶牛走进棚子开始，落到摆满奶酪的柜台。

normal.en: Dairy began as a woman's job and ended as a whole industry.
normal.cn: dairy 从一个女人的活计开始，最后成了一整个行业。

normal.en: Milk cannot wait, so the dairy must be near the cow.
normal.cn: 奶等不起，所以奶牛场得离牛很近。

normal.en: Dairy and diary differ by one letter and by a whole day.
normal.cn: dairy 和 diary 只差一个字母，也差着一整天的记录。

normal.en: A dairy counter is a farm seen through glass.
normal.cn: 乳品柜台，就是隔着玻璃看到的一座农场。

normal.en: If it comes from a cow and is white, it may be dairy.
normal.cn: 如果它来自奶牛又是白色的，那可能就是乳制品。

abstract.en: Picture a row of cows waiting at a low door.
abstract.cn: 想象一排奶牛在一道矮门前等着。

abstract.en: Picture a steel can of milk breathing steam.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钢桶里的牛奶冒着热气。

abstract.en: Picture a glass case of yellow butter blocks.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃柜里一块块黄色的黄油。

examples.en: The dairy sends fresh milk to the town each morning.
examples.cn: 这个奶牛场每天早上把鲜奶送到镇上。

examples.en: He bought butter at the dairy.
examples.cn: 他在乳品店买了黄油。

examples.en: The dairy counter was full of cheese.
examples.cn: 乳品柜台摆满了奶酪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dairy 记成「奶棚」：天一亮奶牛进棚，挤出的奶就在这个 dairy 里变成黄油和奶酪。

root: 源自古英语 dæge（女仆），她原先管揉面，后来也管挤奶与做奶制品；地方名 dey 逐渐演变为 dairy，指产奶、存奶与卖奶的场所。

sensesIntro.en: From the farm that produces milk, to the shop that sells it, to the label on the products themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: 从产奶的农场，到卖奶的店铺，再到奶制品本身的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cows filing into a shed where milk is collected.
core.cn: 核心意象：奶牛排队走进收集牛奶的棚子。

branches.en: The first place is the farm or shed where milk is kept.
branches.cn: 最初的场所，是存放牛奶的农场或棚屋。

branches.en: The same word names the shop that sells the milk.
branches.cn: 同一个词也指卖奶的店铺。

branches.en: As a label it marks butter, cheese, and cream.
branches.cn: 作为标签，它标出黄油、奶酪和奶油。

branches.en: The farm and the shop are two ends of one route.
branches.cn: 农场和店铺，是同一条路的两端。

branches.en: A shop and its goods can share a single name.
branches.cn: 店铺和它的货物，可以共用一个名字。

intro.en: Dairy has a small English family, all of it tied to milk and to the work of producing it.
intro.cn: dairy 的英语词族不大，全都和牛奶以及产奶的活计有关。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin root; it comes from Old English dæge, a woman servant.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 dæge（女仆）。

items.exampleCN: 这个山谷有三座奶牛场。
乳品业养活了整个村子。

items.meaning: a man who works with milk
items.exampleCN: 奶场工人天没亮就起来了。

items.example: The dairy farm has eighty cows.
items.exampleCN: 这座奶牛场有八十头奶牛。

items.example: The dairy cattle graze on the hill.

items.exampleCN: 她选了一份不含乳制品的甜点。

definition_en: a raised platform at the front of a hall for speakers or honoured guests
core_image: 大厅尽头一方抬高的木台，话筒与姓名牌排在台面上
scene: 校长走上讲台开始致辞。The headmaster stepped onto the dais and began his speech.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：dais 指大厅前方抬高的讲台；句意是校长走上讲台致辞。

senses.title: Speaker platform
senses.definition: a low raised platform for a speaker or a teacher
senses.definitionCN: 供演讲者或教师使用的低矮高台
senses.example: She spoke from the dais without notes.
senses.exampleCN: 她站在讲台上脱稿发言。
senses.why: A wooden step with a microphone on it.
senses.whyCN: 一级放着话筒的木台。

senses.title: Honour seat
senses.definition: the raised place where honoured guests sit at a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 典礼上贵宾就座的抬高席位
senses.example: The winners sat on the dais beside the mayor.
senses.exampleCN: 获奖者与市长一同坐在主席台上。
senses.why: A row of name cards above the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 人群上方一排姓名牌。

intro.en: Dais comes from Old French deis, a raised table, from Latin discus, a round plate.
intro.cn: dais 源自古法语 deis（高台桌），再溯至拉丁语 discus（圆盘）。

items.en: Discus meant a round plate or a quoit.
items.cn: discus 意为圆盘或铁饼。

items.en: Discus also named a high table in a hall.
items.cn: discus 也指厅中的高桌。

items.en: Deis named the raised table of honour.
items.cn: deis 指尊位的高桌。

items.en: Deis entered English as a hall platform.
items.cn: 十三世纪 deis 作为厅中高台进入英语。

items.en: Dais became the standard spelling.
items.cn: 十六世纪 dais 成为标准拼法。

items.en: Dais now names any speaker platform.
items.cn: 二十世纪 dais 泛指任何演讲高台。

note.en: The look-alike group swaps one letter; the near-meaning group names other raised speaking places.
note.cn: 形近组只换一个字母；近义组是其他抬高的发言处。

entries.definition: A small white flower with a yellow centre.
A small stand a speaker stands behind.

normalIntro.en: Dais sounds like daisy: a flower standing one step above the grass.
normalIntro.cn: dais 听起来像 daisy：一朵高出草地一级的花。

normal.en: A daisy grows a little above the grass.
normal.cn: 雏菊长得比草高一点。

normal.en: A dais stands a little above the floor.
normal.cn: 讲台比地面高一点。

normal.en: Both are raised and both are seen.
normal.cn: 两者都抬高，都被看见。

normal.en: The speaker stands on the dais.
normal.cn: 演讲者站在讲台上。

normal.en: The guests sit on the top dais.
normal.cn: 贵宾坐在主宾高台上。

abstract.en: A wooden step with a microphone on it.
abstract.cn: 一级放着话筒的木台。

abstract.en: A row of name cards above the crowd.
abstract.cn: 人群上方一排姓名牌。

abstract.en: A flower one step above the grass.
abstract.cn: 一朵高出草地一级的花。

examples.en: The dais was covered with a red cloth.
examples.cn: 讲台上铺着红布。

examples.en: Please keep the dais clear for the speakers.
examples.cn: 请为演讲者保持讲台畅通。

examples.en: She walked down from the dais to the floor.
examples.cn: 她从讲台走下来到地面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「戴斯」——戴上麦克风的那一级台阶；与 daisy（雏菊）只差一个字母。

root: 拉丁 discus（圆盘）→ 古法语 deis（高桌）→ 中古英语 deis → dais

sensesIntro.en: One raised board: speaking and honour.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一块抬高的木板：发言与尊位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden step lifting a voice above a hall
core.cn: 核心意象：一级把声音托举到厅堂之上的木台

branches.en: A wooden step with a microphone on it.
branches.cn: 一级放着话筒的木台。

branches.en: A row of name cards above the crowd.
branches.cn: 人群上方一排姓名牌。

branches.en: One board, two kinds of height.
branches.cn: 同一块木板，两种高度。

branches.en: A flower one step above the grass.
branches.cn: 一朵高出草地一级的花。

branches.en: A seat that everyone can see.
branches.cn: 一个所有人都看得见的座位。

intro.en: Dais is a borrowing from discus; its neighbours share the raised-place roots.
intro.cn: dais 是从 discus 借来的词；相邻词共享「抬高之处」的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin discus means a round plate and podium means a raised place.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 discus 意为圆盘，podium 意为抬高之处。

definition_en: harm done to something, or to harm it
core_image: 冰雹在车顶砸出一片细小的坑
scene: 冰雹过后，车顶多了一片密密麻麻的小坑。The hail damaged every car on the street.
sceneCN: 这里 damaged 是 damage 的过去式，指「损坏」（第 2 个义项：使东西受损）；句意是冰雹砸坏了街上每一辆车。

senses.title: Harm done to a thing
senses.definition: physical harm that makes something less useful or sound
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变得不好用或不完整的实体损伤
senses.example: The storm caused damage to the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨给屋顶造成了损坏。
senses.why: A thing is damaged when it can no longer do its job.
senses.whyCN: 当一个东西干不了它的活，它就是被损坏了。

senses.title: To harm something
senses.definition: to harm something or make it worse
senses.definitionCN: 伤害某物或使其状况变差
senses.example: The hail damaged every car on the street.
senses.exampleCN: 冰雹砸坏了街上每一辆车。
senses.why: Damage is what the blow leaves behind on the surface.
senses.whyCN: 损坏，就是那一击在表面上留下的东西。

senses.title: Money paid for harm
senses.definition: money paid to repair or make up for harm, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 为修复或弥补损害而支付的钱，通常用复数
senses.example: The court ordered him to pay damages.
senses.exampleCN: 法院命令他支付赔偿金。
senses.why: When a thing cannot be mended, money is asked to stand in for it.
senses.whyCN: 东西修不好时，就请钱来代替它。

intro.en: Damage comes from Latin damnum, loss or cost, through Old French damage.
intro.cn: damage 源自拉丁语 damnum（损失、代价），经古法语 damage 进入英语。

items.en: Damnum meant loss, cost, or harm.
items.cn: damnum 意为损失、代价或伤害。

items.en: Damnare meant to cause a loss or condemn.
items.cn: damnare 意为使受损失或宣判。

items.en: Damage named harm and the loss it caused.
items.cn: damage 指伤害以及它带来的损失。

items.en: Damage entered English for injury to property.
items.cn: damage 进入英语，指对财物的损伤。

items.en: The plural damages named money paid in law.
items.cn: 复数 damages 指法律上支付的赔偿金。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dam- opening, and the meaning group names other kinds of harm.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dam- 开头，近义组列出其他形式的伤害。

entries.definition: a wall that holds back water
injury or damage to someone or something
the fact of no longer having something

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with hail on a car roof and end with a court order to pay.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从砸在车顶的冰雹开始，落到法院的赔付命令。

normal.en: Damage is the bill the world sends after a blow.
normal.cn: 损坏，是世界在打击之后寄来的账单。

normal.en: A thing is damaged when it stops doing what it was made for.
normal.cn: 东西做不了它原本该做的事，就是损坏了。

normal.en: Reputation can be damaged without a single broken object.
normal.cn: 名声可以被损害，却一件东西都没碎。

normal.en: When repair is impossible, damages are money in its place.
normal.cn: 修不好时，赔偿金就是代替它的钱。

normal.en: If it costs something to fix, there was damage.
normal.cn: 如果修它要花钱，那就是有过损坏。

abstract.en: Picture a car roof covered in small round dents.
abstract.cn: 想象车顶布满一个个小圆坑。

abstract.en: Picture a cracked window that still keeps out rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇裂了却还能挡雨的窗。

abstract.en: Picture a folded paper with a sum written at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折起来的纸，末尾写着一个数额。

examples.en: The storm caused damage to the roof.
examples.cn: 暴风雨给屋顶造成了损坏。

examples.en: The hail damaged every car on the street.
examples.cn: 冰雹砸坏了街上每一辆车。

examples.en: The court ordered him to pay damages.
examples.cn: 法院命令他支付赔偿金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 damage 记成「打折」：东西被打折了，就是受了损；修不好，就用钱来赔。

root: 源自拉丁语 damnum（损失、代价），经古法语 damage 进入英语；本义是让人遭受损失，先指财物的损伤，后指法律上为弥补损失而支付的赔偿金。

sensesIntro.en: From the harm a blow leaves, to the act of harming, to the money that stands in for what was lost.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一击留下的损伤，到使人受损的动作，再到代替损失的那笔钱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard blow landing on a surface and leaving a mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次重击落在表面上，留下痕迹。

branches.en: The noun names the harm itself.
branches.cn: 名词指伤害本身。

branches.en: The verb names the act that produces it.
branches.cn: 动词指造成它的那个动作。

branches.en: The plural turns the harm into a sum of money.
branches.cn: 复数把伤害变成一笔钱。

branches.en: The harm and the harming are two sides of one event.
branches.cn: 损伤与造成损伤，是同一件事的两面。

branches.en: What cannot be repaired is paid for instead.
branches.cn: 修不好的部分，就用钱来抵。

intro.en: Damage belongs to the Latin damnum family, where loss turns into harm and into money paid.
intro.cn: damage 属于拉丁语 damnum 这一族，「损失」在这里变成伤害与赔款。

latinIntro.en: The Latin damnum, loss, and damnare, to condemn, stand behind this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 damnum（损失）与 damnare（宣判）是这一族词的根。

items.example: The damage was easy to see.

items.exampleCN: 破损的箱子被退了回来。

items.example: They damned the plan as foolish.
items.exampleCN: 他们谴责这个计划愚蠢。

items.example: The old tale warned of damnation.
items.exampleCN: 那个古老的故事警告人会有永罚。

items.example: He spoke damagingly of his rival.
items.exampleCN: 他说了有害于对手的话。
水灾损失导致道路封闭。

definition_en: slightly wet, usually in a cold and unpleasant way
core_image: 晾了一夜没收的毛巾，摸上去又凉又潮
scene: 雨停之后，墙角的砖摸上去又凉又潮。The walls felt damp after the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 damp 指「潮湿的」（第 1 个义项：微微发潮发冷）；句意是雨后墙壁摸上去发潮。

senses.title: Slightly wet and cold
senses.definition: holding just enough water to feel cold and unpleasantly wet
senses.definitionCN: 含着一点水，摸起来又冷又不舒服
senses.example: The towel was still damp when I picked it up.
senses.exampleCN: 我拿起毛巾时，它还是潮的。
senses.why: The wetness is small, but the cold makes it impossible to ignore.
senses.whyCN: 水并不多，可那股凉意让人无法忽略。

senses.title: Moisture in air or wall
senses.definition: water held in the air or inside a solid material
senses.definitionCN: 藏在空气里或墙体内部的水分
senses.example: Damp had crept up the wall behind the cupboard.
senses.exampleCN: 潮气顺着柜子后面的墙往上爬。
senses.why: When water has no shape of its own, we name it as a presence.
senses.whyCN: 水没有自己的形状时，我们就把它当作一种存在来称呼。

senses.title: To make less strong
senses.definition: to reduce the strength of a flame, a sound, or a feeling
senses.definitionCN: 降低火势、声音或情绪的力量
senses.example: They damped the flames with wet cloths.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用湿布压住了火苗。
senses.why: Covering a fire with something wet is the oldest way to slow it.
senses.whyCN: 用湿的东西盖住火，是最古老的灭火办法。

intro.en: Damp came into English from Low German, where it first meant vapour rather than the wetness vapour leaves behind.
intro.cn: damp 来自低地德语，最初指水汽，而不是水汽留下的潮湿。

items.en: Damp named the vapour that rises from wet ground.
items.cn: damp 指湿地上冒起的水汽。

items.en: The word entered English for a mist that wets whatever it touches.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语，指碰到什么就把什么弄湿的雾气。

items.en: Damp shifted from the mist itself to the slight wetness left behind.
items.cn: damp 从雾气本身转指雾气留下的那点潮湿。

items.en: Damp down appeared, meaning to cover a fire so it burns slowly.
items.cn: 出现了 damp down，指盖住火让它慢慢烧。

items.en: Damp now mostly describes cold, unwelcome wetness in cloth or walls.
items.cn: 如今 damp 多形容布或墙上那种阴冷、不受欢迎的潮。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by a single letter, and the meaning group moves from mild wetness to soaked.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母，近义组则从轻微潮湿一路走到湿透。

entries.definition: a wall built across a river to hold water back
entries.definitionCN: 横在河上拦水的一道坝

entries.definition: slightly wet in a soft, often pleasant way
entries.definitionCN: 微微湿润，常带柔和、舒服的意味

entries.definition: having a lot of water vapour in the air

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a towel that never dried and end with a fire being covered.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一条没晾干的毛巾开始，落到一堆被盖住的火。

normal.en: A towel left in the bathroom keeps the cold of the water that soaked it.
normal.cn: 忘在浴室里的毛巾，留着浸过它的那股凉。

normal.en: A damp wall writes its history in dark patches.
normal.cn: 潮湿的墙用深色的斑块写自己的历史。

normal.en: Damp air makes a coat feel heavier than it is.
normal.cn: 潮湿的空气让外套摸起来比实际更沉。

normal.en: Cover a fire with wet cloth and the flame goes quiet.
normal.cn: 用湿布盖住火，火苗就安静下来。

normal.en: If the cold comes with the water, damp is the word you want.
normal.cn: 如果凉意跟着水一起来，你要的词就是 damp。

abstract.en: Picture a cold hand pressed to a stone wall in autumn.
abstract.cn: 想象秋天里一只冰凉的手按在石墙上。

abstract.en: Picture steam rising where the sun hits wet ground.
abstract.cn: 想象太阳照在湿地上，水汽升起来。

abstract.en: Picture a wet cloth dropped over a small flame.
abstract.cn: 想象一块湿布盖在一小簇火上。

examples.en: The walls felt damp after the rain.
examples.cn: 雨后墙壁摸上去发潮。

examples.en: She wiped the table with a damp cloth.
examples.cn: 她用一块湿布擦了桌子。

examples.en: They damped down the fire before leaving the camp.
examples.cn: 离开营地前他们把火压小了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 damp 记成「潮」：字母 d 像一滴水，amp 像插头，插头受了潮就会发闷。

root: 源自古低地德语 damp（水汽），十四世纪进入英语，先指湿地上冒的雾气，十六世纪转为指雾气留下的那点湿冷；十八世纪起又有「压住火」的用法，潮湿与压灭其实是同一个动作的两面。

sensesIntro.en: From a cold wet surface, to the moisture hidden in a wall, to a fire covered until it dies.
sensesIntro.cn: 从湿冷的表面，到墙里藏着的潮气，再到被盖住而渐熄的火。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cold, slightly wet surface touched by the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：手掌触到一片阴凉微湿的表面。

branches.en: A towel or wall that holds a little cold water is the first picture.
branches.cn: 含着一点冷水、摸起来发凉的毛巾或墙，是第一幅画面。

branches.en: The same water, when it hides in air or plaster, becomes a presence.
branches.cn: 同样的水藏进空气或墙灰里，就成了一种存在。

branches.en: Wetness laid over a flame takes its strength away.
branches.cn: 湿的东西盖到火上，就把火的力量拿走了。

branches.en: The wet surface and the hidden moisture are one water in two places.
branches.cn: 表面的湿和藏着的潮，是同一份水待在两个地方。

branches.en: Both senses are about water winning slowly, without force.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是水在慢慢地赢，不靠蛮力。

intro.en: Damp is a small family: the adjective, its verbs of wetting and slowing, and a set of compound labels.
intro.cn: damp 这一族不大：一个形容词、几个表示弄湿和减弱的动词，还有一批复合标签。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here; the word came from Low German damp, meaning vapour.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，它来自低地德语的 damp（水汽）。

items.example: The dampness in the room never left.

items.meaning: a thing that reduces sound or spirit
items.example: Rain put a damper on the picnic.
The coat hung damply by the door.
They laid a damp-proof sheet under the floor.
items.exampleCN: 他们在地板下铺了防潮层。

items.meaning: to cover a fire or calm a feeling
items.example: He damped down his anger and spoke calmly.
items.exampleCN: 他压下怒气，平静地说话。

items.meaning: a layer that stops water rising in a wall
items.example: The old house has no damp course.
items.exampleCN: 这栋老房子没有防潮层。

definition_zh: v. 使潮湿；使沮丧；抑制（热情、需求等）
definition_en: to make something slightly wet, or to make a feeling or activity less strong
core_image: 一块湿布轻轻按在额头上，热气与火气一起被压下去
scene: 她用水把布打湿再敷上去。She dampened the cloth before laying it on the forehead.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：dampen 指使微湿；句意是她先把布打湿再敷在额头上。

senses.title: Make wet
senses.definition: to make something slightly wet
senses.definitionCN: 使某物微微变湿
senses.example: Dampen the soil before sowing.
senses.exampleCN: 播种前先把土壤润湿。
senses.why: A wet cloth pressed on a warm forehead.
senses.whyCN: 一块湿布按在发热的额头上。

senses.title: Reduce feeling
senses.definition: to make a feeling such as hope less strong
senses.definitionCN: 使希望等情绪减弱
senses.example: The rain dampened our spirits.
senses.exampleCN: 那场雨让我们扫兴。
senses.why: A bright balloon losing its air.
senses.whyCN: 一只正在泄气的亮色气球。

senses.title: Restrict growth
senses.definition: to hold back demand, noise or vibration
senses.definitionCN: 抑制需求、噪声或振动
senses.example: Higher rates dampen demand for houses.
senses.exampleCN: 利率上升抑制购房需求。
senses.why: A hand laid flat on a ringing bell.
senses.whyCN: 一只按在鸣钟上的手。

intro.cn: dampen 由 damp 加动词词尾 -en 构成，意为「使变潮」。

items.en: Damp meant vapour or steam.
items.cn: damp 意为蒸气或水汽。

definition_zh: adj. 阴湿的；湿冷的（令人不快）
definition_en: unpleasantly damp and cold, especially of an enclosed place
core_image: 地窖石壁上挂着一层水汽，空气又冷又黏
scene: 地窖里又黑又湿冷。The cellar was dark and dank.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：dank 指阴冷潮湿；句意是地窖又黑又湿冷。

senses.title: Cold and wet
senses.definition: unpleasantly cold and damp in an enclosed space
senses.definitionCN: 封闭空间里令人不快地又冷又湿
senses.example: The tunnel smelled dank and earthy.

senses.why: Stone walls wearing a film of water.

senses.title: Chilling mood
senses.definition: making a place feel gloomy and unwelcoming
senses.definitionCN: 使一个地方显得阴沉而不受欢迎
senses.example: The empty house had a dank silence.
senses.exampleCN: 那栋空屋有一种阴冷的寂静。
senses.why: A cold room nobody wants to enter.

intro.en: Dank is probably from a Scandinavian word for wet and cold.
intro.cn: dank 可能源自斯堪的纳维亚语中表示湿冷的词。

items.cn: 一个北方词指又湿又冷。

items.cn: dank 在中古英语中表示湿冷。

items.cn: 十八世纪 dank 成为「令人不快的潮湿」的固定词。

items.cn: 十九世纪 dank 扩展到形容阴沉的房间。

normalIntro.en: Dank looks like dark plus bank: a dark river bank under a stone.
normalIntro.cn: dank 看起来像 dark 加 bank：石头下一条黑暗的河岸。

normal.en: Dark means without light.
normal.cn: dark 意为没有光。

normal.en: A bank can be cold and wet.
normal.cn: 河岸可能又冷又湿。

normal.en: Dank is the dark wet corner.
normal.cn: dank 就是那个又黑又湿的角落。

normal.en: A cellar is often dank.
normal.cn: 地窖常常阴湿。

normal.en: Dank air feels heavy on the skin.
normal.cn: 阴湿的空气贴在皮肤上发沉。

examples.cn: 阴湿的地下室毁掉了存放的书。

examples.en: We left the dank cave and walked into the sun.
examples.cn: 我们离开湿冷的洞穴，走进阳光里。

examples.en: A dank smell rose from the old well.
examples.cn: 一股阴湿的气味从古井里升起。

sensesIntro.cn: 同一种湿冷：在石头上，也在气氛里。

core.cn: 核心意象：一间呼出冷水的石窖

branches.en: Stone walls wearing a film of water.

definition_en: to be brave enough to do something difficult or risky
core_image: 站在跳水台边缘，脚尖探出去又收回来
scene: 他站在跳板尽头，深吸一口气才迈出去。No one dared to jump from the high board.
sceneCN: 这里 dare 指「敢」（第 1 个义项：有勇气去做）；句意是没人敢从那块高板上跳下去。

senses.title: Be brave enough to act
senses.definition: to have enough courage to do something you fear
senses.definitionCN: 有足够的勇气去做自己害怕的事
senses.example: No one dared to jump from the high board.
senses.exampleCN: 没人敢从那块高板上跳下去。
senses.why: The word measures courage against a fear that is already present.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是在已经存在的恐惧面前，量一量勇气够不够。

senses.title: Challenge someone to try
senses.definition: to urge someone to do something risky by calling them afraid
senses.definitionCN: 用「你怕了」来挑动别人去做有风险的事
senses.example: They dared him to sing in front of the class.
senses.exampleCN: 他们激他在全班面前唱歌。
senses.why: To dare another is to hand your own courage over as a test.
senses.whyCN: 去激别人，就是把自己的勇气当作考题递过去。

intro.en: Dare goes back to Old English durran, an old verb that has kept its shape for a thousand years.
intro.cn: dare 可上溯到古英语 durran，这个古老动词的形状一千年几乎没变。

items.en: Durran meant to have courage for something feared.
items.cn: durran 意为对害怕之事仍有勇气。

items.en: The past tense dorste kept an older pattern of vowel change.
items.cn: 过去式 dorste 保留了更古老的元音变化规律。

items.en: The verb split into a full verb and a helper in questions and denials.
items.cn: 这个动词分成两类：实义动词，以及疑问和否定里的助动词。

items.en: The sense of challenging another person became common.
items.cn: 「挑动别人」的用法变得常见。

items.en: Dare survives mainly in set phrases and in the speech of the brave.
items.cn: 如今 dare 主要活在固定短语和勇敢者的嘴里。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the long vowel and final r, and the meaning group names ways of facing risk.
note.cn: 形近组共享长元音和词尾 r，近义组则列出面对风险的不同方式。

entries.definition: to go somewhere or do something risky
to put something valuable in danger
to face something fearful on purpose

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a foot at the edge of a board and end with a voice saying try it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从跳板边缘的一只脚开始，落到一句「你试试」的声音。

normal.en: To dare is to move while the fear stays where it is.
normal.cn: 敢，就是恐惧原地不动，人却往前走了。

normal.en: The board is only high because the ground is far below.
normal.cn: 跳板之所以高，只因为地面在很远的下方。

normal.en: A dare from a friend is a test wrapped in a joke.
normal.cn: 朋友的一句激将，是用玩笑包着的考试。

normal.en: Dare not is the shortest way to say I am afraid.
normal.cn: dare not 是说出「我怕」最短的方式。

normal.en: Courage is measured by what it costs, not by the noise it makes.
normal.cn: 勇气看代价，不看响声。

abstract.en: Picture a toe testing the cold air beyond the board.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚趾试探跳板外的冷空气。

abstract.en: Picture a child pushed forward by a circle of friends.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子被一圈朋友推到前面。

abstract.en: Picture the second after the jump, when there is no way back.
abstract.cn: 想象跳下之后的第二秒，已无路可退。

examples.en: No one dared to jump from the high board.
examples.cn: 没人敢从那块高板上跳下去。

examples.en: She did not dare look back at the door.
examples.cn: 她不敢回头看那扇门。

examples.en: He dared his brother to eat the hot pepper.
examples.cn: 他激他弟弟去吃那根辣椒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dare 记成「往前一跺」：d 是脚，are 是「是」，脚一跺说「我敢」，就是 dare。

root: 源自古英语 durran（敢），属日耳曼语系古老的过去—现在动词，过去式 dorste 保留元音变化；中古英语时分成实义动词与疑问否定中的助动词，十六世纪又发展出「激将」之义。

sensesIntro.en: From a person finding courage inside, to a person handing a test to someone else.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个人在内心找到勇气，到把一场考试递到别人手里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot at the edge of a diving board.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚踩在跳板边缘。

branches.en: The first sense is the inward push that beats the fear.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是压过恐惧的那股内在推力。

branches.en: The second sense moves that push into the mouth of another person.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把那股推力放进另一个人的嘴里。

branches.en: Both senses test courage, one on yourself and one on a friend.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在考验勇气，一个考自己，一个考朋友。

branches.en: A challenge only works if the other person already wants to be brave.
branches.cn: 激将之所以有效，是因为对方本来就想做个勇敢的人。

branches.en: The same word covers the jump and the voice that orders it.
branches.cn: 同一个词既管那一跳，也管命令人跳的那把声音。

intro.en: Dare is a short, old family: the verb, its noun of courage, and a few tightly fixed phrases.
intro.cn: dare 这一族又短又老：一个动词、一个表勇气的名词，还有几个扣得很紧的短语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin here; dare is a native Germanic verb that has stayed close to its Old English form.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语；dare 是本族日耳曼动词，一直保留着接近古英语的形态。

items.meaning: a person who takes wild risks

items.meaning: a stronger challenge to do something
items.example: He gave his friend a double dare.
items.exampleCN: 他给朋友下了双倍的激将。

definition_en: to run somewhere very quickly, or a small quick movement
core_image: 一个人低着头冲向雨中的公交站
scene: 雨忽然大了，他一路冲向街对面的屋檐。He dashed across the road to the shelter.
sceneCN: 这里 dash 指「猛冲」（第 1 个义项：快速奔跑）；句意是他冲过马路跑到避雨处。

senses.title: Run with sudden speed
senses.definition: to move somewhere very quickly and without delay
senses.definitionCN: 飞快地、不耽搁地赶到某处
senses.example: He dashed across the road to the shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 他冲过马路跑到避雨处。
senses.why: A dash is short and urgent; it ends as soon as the goal is reached.
senses.whyCN: 猛冲又短又急，一到目的地就结束。

senses.title: A mark on the page
senses.definition: a short line used in writing to show a break or a jump
senses.definitionCN: 书写中用来表示停顿或跳跃的一道短线
senses.example: He put a dash between the two dates.
senses.exampleCN: 他在两个日期之间加了一道破折号。
senses.why: The pen moves fast, so the mark itself looks like a dash.
senses.whyCN: 笔走得快，画出的痕迹也像一次猛冲。

senses.title: A very small amount
senses.definition: a small quantity thrown into something else
senses.definitionCN: 随手加进另一样东西里的一点点
senses.example: Add a dash of vinegar to the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 往汤里加一点醋。
senses.why: The amount is thrown in quickly, as a cook throws in salt.
senses.whyCN: 那点分量是随手甩进去的，就像厨师撒盐。

intro.en: Dash probably began as a word that imitated the sound and force of a blow.
intro.cn: dash 最初大概是一个模仿撞击声与力道的词。

items.en: The word echoed the noise of something struck hard.
items.cn: 这个词模仿硬物被击中的声响。

items.en: Dashen meant to strike or knock something violently.
items.cn: dashen 意为猛击或猛撞某物。

items.en: The sense of moving fast replaced the sense of striking.
items.cn: 「快速移动」的意思取代了「猛击」的意思。

items.en: The noun named the little line a quick pen leaves behind.
items.cn: 名词开始指快笔留下的一道短线。

items.en: A dash of salt meant the amount a cook throws in at once.
items.cn: a dash of salt 指厨师一次甩进去的那点分量。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel, and the meaning group names faster and slower ways to move.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音，近义组则按快慢排列移动方式。

entries.definition: a long strip of cloth worn round the waist
to move with great speed and haste
to run at full speed for a short distance
to move suddenly like a thrown spear
entries.definitionCN: 像掷出的矛一样突然移动

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a foot pushing off wet ground and end with a pinch of salt falling into soup.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从湿地上蹬出的一只脚开始，落到落进汤里的一撮盐。

normal.en: A dash is a run that refuses to last.
normal.cn: 猛冲是一场不肯持续太久的奔跑。

normal.en: The mark on the page is the path of a pen in a hurry.
normal.cn: 纸上那道记号，是一支赶路的笔留下的轨迹。

normal.en: A dash of salt is speed measured in taste.
normal.cn: 一小撮盐，是用味道量出来的速度。

normal.en: When the rain starts, everyone discovers they can run.
normal.cn: 雨一下，人人都发现自己会跑。

normal.en: One word holds the runner, the mark, and the pinch.
normal.cn: 一个词同时装着奔跑的人、纸上的记号和一撮的分量。

abstract.en: Picture a figure bent forward against the rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一个弓着身子顶雨前行的人影。

abstract.en: Picture a pen pulled across paper and leaving a straight scar.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔划过纸面，留下一道直直的痕。

abstract.en: Picture a cook shaking salt once over a pot.
abstract.cn: 想象厨师在锅上抖一下盐。

examples.en: He dashed across the road to the shelter.
examples.cn: 他冲过马路跑到避雨处。

examples.en: Add a dash of vinegar to the soup.
examples.cn: 往汤里加一点醋。

examples.en: She dashed off a note before the meeting.
examples.cn: 开会前她匆匆写了一张便条。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dash 记成「哒嘘」：跑起来脚下「哒」一声，嘴里「嘘」一口气，一冲就到。

root: 中古英语 daschen 出现于十三世纪，最初模仿猛击的声响与力道，意为「猛撞」；十六世纪转为「快速移动」，十七世纪又指笔下划过的一道短线，十八世纪起再引申为「一小撮」的分量。

sensesIntro.en: From a body thrown forward, to a mark left by a quick pen, to a pinch thrown into a pot.
sensesIntro.cn: 从向前甩出去的身体，到快笔留下的一道痕，再到甩进锅里的一撮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person running hard through sudden rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人顶着骤雨拼命奔跑。

branches.en: The first sense is the whole body moving at speed.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是整个身体高速移动。

branches.en: The second is the same speed reduced to a pen stroke.
branches.cn: 第二个把同样的速度缩小成一道笔画。

branches.en: The third is the same quick gesture applied to a powder.
branches.cn: 第三个把同样快速的手势用在粉末上。

branches.en: Both the runner and the pen cross a space without stopping.
branches.cn: 奔跑的人和笔都不停顿地穿过一段距离。

branches.en: A short line and a small amount are both things cut short.
branches.cn: 一道短线和一小撮，都是被截短的东西。

intro.en: Dash is a short family: a verb, an adjective of style, and compounds that grew from speed.
intro.cn: dash 这一族不长：一个动词、一个形容风度的形容词，还有几个从速度长出来的复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; dash is an English word of imitative origin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，dash 是英语中模仿声音造出来的词。

items.example: She dashed to catch the train.
He looked dashing in the old coat.
items.exampleCN: 他穿那件旧外套显得很潇洒。

items.example: The keys lay on the dashboard.
He made a dash for the door.
Use an em dash for the aside.

definition_en: a large set of information stored in a computer and arranged for quick searching
core_image: 一间排满文件柜、每格都贴着编号的房间
scene: 前台一输入名字，屏幕上立刻跳出档案。The database found her record in seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 database 指「数据库」（第 1 个义项：有结构地存放数据的系统）；句意是数据库几秒内就找到了她的记录。

senses.title: An organized store of data
senses.definition: a large body of information arranged so that it can be searched quickly
senses.definitionCN: 按一定方式排列、便于快速检索的大量信息
senses.example: The database found her record in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 数据库几秒内就找到了她的记录。
senses.why: The power lies not in the amount of data but in the order it is kept in.
senses.whyCN: 力量不在数据多少，而在它们被放得多有次序。

senses.title: The software that runs it
senses.definition: the program or system that stores and answers questions about such data
senses.definitionCN: 负责存放数据并回答查询的程序或系统
senses.example: The team installed a new database last month.
senses.exampleCN: 团队上个月装了新的数据库系统。
senses.why: We use one word for the store and for the machine that guards it.
senses.whyCN: 我们用一个词同时指这座仓库和看守它的机器。

intro.en: Database is a modern coinage joining data, the plural of Latin datum, to base, a foundation.
intro.cn: database 是现代的造词，把拉丁语 datum 的复数 data（数据）与 base（基础）拼在一起。

items.en: Datum meant something given, a fact handed over.
items.cn: datum 意为「被给出的东西」，即交出的事实。

items.en: Data entered English as the plural of datum.
items.cn: data 作为 datum 的复数进入英语。

items.en: Data bank named a store of facts kept for later use.
items.cn: data bank 指为日后使用而存放事实的库。

items.en: Database was coined for computer files that could be searched.
items.cn: database 被造出来，指可检索的计算机文件集合。

items.en: Database now covers everything from a phone list to a national registry.
items.cn: 如今 database 从电话簿一直指到国家登记系统。

note.en: The look-alike group breaks the compound into its parts, and the meaning group names other collections of records.
note.cn: 形近组把这个复合词拆成部件，近义组则列出其他形式的记录集合。

entries.definition: facts and figures collected for use
entries.definitionCN: 为使用而收集的事实与数字

entries.definition: the bottom or starting point of something
a store of old records kept for reference
entries.definitionCN: 为查考而保存旧记录的地方

entries.definition: an official list kept in order
a book of records kept in rows

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a wall of numbered drawers and end with an answer appearing in a second.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一面编号抽屉的墙开始，落到一秒内跳出来的答案。

normal.en: A database is a library where no book is out of place.
normal.cn: 数据库是一座没有一本书放错位置的图书馆。

normal.en: Order is the only thing that makes a million facts useful.
normal.cn: 让一百万条事实变得有用的，只有次序。

normal.en: The word joins what is given to the ground it stands on.
normal.cn: 这个词把「被给出的东西」接到了「它立足的地基」上。

normal.en: A question asked well is already half an answer.
normal.cn: 问得好的问题，已经是一半的答案。

normal.en: Every record is a person who once filled in a form.
normal.cn: 每条记录背后，都是一个曾经填过表的人。

abstract.en: Picture a long room of grey cabinets with small labels.
abstract.cn: 想象一间长屋子，摆满贴着小标签的灰色柜子。

abstract.en: Picture a cursor blinking beside an empty search box.
abstract.cn: 想象一个空搜索框旁闪烁的光标。

abstract.en: Picture one line of text rising to the top of a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一行字升到屏幕最上方。

examples.en: The database found her record in seconds.
examples.cn: 数据库几秒内就找到了她的记录。

examples.en: All the patient records are kept in one database.
examples.cn: 所有病人记录都存在同一个数据库里。

examples.en: They built a database of local plant names.
examples.cn: 他们建了一个本地植物名称的数据库。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 database 记成「数据基地」：data 是数据，base 是基地，数据存放的基地就是数据库。

root: 由 data（数据，拉丁语 datum「被给出之物」的复数）与 base（基础、基地）复合而成，二十世纪六十年代随计算机检索系统出现，指按结构存放、便于查询的大量信息。

sensesIntro.en: From the ordered store of facts, to the system that keeps answering for it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从按序存放的事实，到替它回答问题的系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room of numbered drawers, each holding one kind of fact.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间编了号的抽屉房，每格装着一种事实。

branches.en: The first sense is the store itself, judged by its order.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是仓库本身，以次序论高低。

branches.en: The second sense is the machine that reads and answers.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是负责读取和回答的机器。

branches.en: The store and the system are named together because neither works alone.
branches.cn: 仓库与系统合称，因为缺了谁都不成。

branches.en: A drawer never answers; the index does.
branches.cn: 抽屉从不回答，回答的是索引。

branches.en: The system is only as good as the order it inherited.
branches.cn: 系统的水平，取决于它继承下来的那套次序。

intro.en: Database is a compound, so its family is built by joining data and base to other words.
intro.cn: database 是个复合词，它的一族靠把 data 与 base 同别的词拼起来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is datum, something given; base is Greek in origin, a step or foundation.
latinIntro.cn: 其中的拉丁成分是 datum（被给出之物）；base 源自希腊语，意为台阶或基础。

items.example: The hospital keeps a databank of scans.
items.exampleCN: 医院存有一个扫描资料库。

items.meaning: software for storing and searching data
the work of keeping a database in order
a database reached through a network
items.example: The journal is in an online database.
items.exampleCN: 这份期刊在一个在线数据库里。

items.meaning: a person who looks after a database
items.example: Only the database administrator can change it.
items.exampleCN: 只有数据库管理员能改动它。

latinEntries.example: Datum is the singular behind data.
latinEntries.exampleCN: datum 是 data 背后的单数形式。

definition_en: a particular day of a month or year, or an arranged meeting
core_image: 日历上用红笔圈出的一个日子
scene: 她翻到日历上圈红的那一天，在旁边写下名字。He wrote the date at the top of the letter.
sceneCN: 这里 date 指「日期」（第 1 个义项：某一天的具体时间）；句意是他在信纸顶部写上了日期。

senses.title: A particular day
senses.definition: the exact day shown by a number, month, and year
senses.definitionCN: 用日、月、年标出的具体某一天
senses.example: He wrote the date at the top of the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 他在信纸顶部写上了日期。
senses.why: A date makes one day stand out from all the others.
senses.whyCN: 日期让某一天从所有日子里站出来。

senses.title: A meeting with someone you like
senses.definition: an arrangement to meet a person you are fond of
senses.definitionCN: 与喜欢的人约定见面
senses.example: They had a date at the little cafe.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在那家小咖啡馆有个约会。
senses.why: The word for a fixed day became the word for a fixed meeting.
senses.whyCN: 表示定好日子的词，后来变成了表示定好见面的词。

senses.title: To have existed since
senses.definition: to show or have a starting point in past time
senses.definitionCN: 显示出或拥有某个过去的时间起点
senses.example: The church dates back to the twelfth century.
senses.exampleCN: 这座教堂可追溯到十二世纪。
senses.why: To date something is to pin it to a day on a long line.
senses.whyCN: 给某物定日期，就是把它钉在一条长线上的某一点。

intro.en: Date comes from Latin data, the word written at the head of a letter to say where and when it was given.
intro.cn: date 来自拉丁语 data，原是在信首注明该信于何时何地「交出」的字样。

items.en: Dare meant to give or hand over.
items.cn: dare 意为给出、交出。

items.en: Letters opened with data, given, followed by the place and day.
items.cn: 信件以 data（交出于）开头，后面写地点与日子。

items.en: French date named the day written on a document.
items.cn: 法语 date 指写在文书上的那一天。

items.en: Date entered English with the same documentary sense.
items.cn: date 以同样的文书含义进入英语。

items.en: The palm fruit had a different origin, named for a finger.
items.cn: 枣这一义项另有来源，因形似手指而得名。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ate shape, and the meaning group names other points and meetings in time.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ate 的词形，近义组则列出时间上的其他节点与相见。

entries.definitionCN: 二十四小时的一段时间

entries.definition: a fixed time arranged for a meeting
a plan that lists times for events
entries.definitionCN: 列出各项活动时间的计划表

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a day circled in red and end with a building that remembers its own beginning.

normal.en: A date turns a plain day into a place you can point at.
normal.cn: 日期把平常的一天，变成你能指出来的一点。

normal.en: The word once sat at the top of a letter, saying this was given today.
normal.cn: 这个词从前坐在信头，说明此信今日交出。

normal.en: Out of date is only time doing its work.
normal.cn: 过时，不过是时间在做它的事。

normal.en: A first date is a whole day shrunk into one hour.
normal.cn: 初次约会，是一整天缩进一小时里。

normal.en: To date a ruin is to give it a birthday.
normal.cn: 给一处遗址定年代，就是给它一个生日。

abstract.en: Picture a red circle on a wall calendar.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上日历里的一个红圈。

abstract.en: Picture two cups on a table and no clock in sight.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上有两只杯子，四下看不见钟。

abstract.en: Picture a stone wall with a carved year above the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一面石墙，门上方刻着年份。

examples.en: He wrote the date at the top of the letter.
examples.cn: 他在信纸顶部写上了日期。

examples.en: The church dates back to the twelfth century.
examples.cn: 这座教堂可追溯到十二世纪。

examples.en: They had a date at the little cafe.
examples.cn: 他们在那家小咖啡馆有个约会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 date 记成「待特」：特别的一天值得等，等到了就是约会，写下来就是日期。

root: 源自拉丁语 data（被交出之物，dare「给出」的过去分词），古时书信开头写 data 再加地点日期；经法语 date 于十四世纪进入英语，先指文书上的日子，后引申为约会与追溯年代。枣的义项另有希腊语来源，与日期无关。

sensesIntro.en: From one marked day, to a meeting fixed on that day, to the day a thing began.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被标记的一天，到定在那天的相见，再到某物开始的那一天。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single day circled in red on a calendar.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上被红笔圈起的一天。

branches.en: The first sense is the plain mark on the calendar.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是日历上那道朴素的记号。

branches.en: The second puts two people on that mark at the same hour.
branches.cn: 第二个把两个人放在那道记号的同一时刻上。

branches.en: The third sends the mark backwards along the years.
branches.cn: 第三个把这道记号沿着年份往回送。

branches.en: A date on paper and a date with a person both mean a fixed point for meeting.
branches.cn: 纸上的日期和与人的约会，都指一个定好的相遇点。

branches.en: To date an object is to write its day in the past.
branches.cn: 给一件东西定年代，就是把它那一天写到过去。

intro.en: Date forms a wide but shallow family, mostly adjectives made with -ed and -able.
intro.cn: date 的一族宽而浅，大多是用 -ed 和 -able 造出的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is dare, to give; data is what has been given.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 dare（给出），data 就是被给出的东西。

items.meaning: marked with a date, or out of fashion
items.example: The letter was dated May first.
items.exampleCN: 那封信注明是五月一日。

items.meaning: having no date written on it
items.example: An undated photo lay on the desk.
items.exampleCN: 桌上有一张未标日期的照片。

items.meaning: able to be given a date
items.example: The coin is datable to the third century.
items.exampleCN: 这枚钱币可定到三世纪。

items.example: She opened her datebook to June.
items.exampleCN: 她翻开记事日历到六月。

items.example: Keep the list up to date.
The map is out of date.
The custom dates back to the war.
items.exampleCN: 这个风俗可追溯到战争年代。

definition_en: a single piece of information used as a basis for reasoning
core_image: 实验记录本上单独的一行读数
scene: 笔记本上只写了一行读数，却是全部测量的起点。One datum was enough to change their conclusion.
sceneCN: 这里 datum 指「数据」（第 1 个义项：单条资料或数值）；句意是一个数据就足以改变他们的结论。

senses.title: One piece of information
senses.definition: a single fact or figure used as a basis for a conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 作为推理依据的单独一条事实或数值
senses.example: One datum was enough to change their conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 一个数据就足以改变他们的结论。
senses.why: The singular keeps its place even when most people say data for one thing.
senses.whyCN: 即使多数人用 data 指一条，单数形式仍守着它的位置。

senses.title: A fixed reference point
senses.definition: a fixed point from which heights or positions are measured
senses.definitionCN: 测量高度或位置时所依据的固定点
senses.example: All heights were taken from the same datum.
senses.exampleCN: 所有高度都从同一个基准点量起。
senses.why: Measuring needs one point that does not move.
senses.whyCN: 要测量，就得有一个不动的点。

intro.en: Datum is Latin for something given, the neuter form of the past participle of dare, to give.
intro.cn: datum 在拉丁语中意为「被给出之物」，是 dare（给出）过去分词的中性形式。

items.en: Dare meant to give, hand over, or grant.
items.cn: dare 意为给出、交出、授予。

items.en: Datum named a thing given, a starting point granted for argument.
items.cn: datum 指被给出之物，即论证时被授予的起点。

items.en: Surveyors used datum for the fixed point of a measurement.
items.cn: 测量师用 datum 指测量的固定基点。

items.en: Scientists took datum into the language of experiment.
items.cn: 科学家把 datum 带进实验的语言。

items.en: The plural data has largely taken over, leaving datum to careful writers.
items.cn: 复数 data 已在多数场合接管，datum 留给讲究用法的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dat- opening, and the meaning group names other single units of knowledge.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dat- 开头，近义组则列出其他单个知识单位。

entries.definition: a particular day of the year
the case of the indirect object
entries.definitionCN: 表示间接宾语的语法格

entries.definition: a number that records an amount
a single number taken from a set of records
entries.definitionCN: 从一组记录中取出的单个数字

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with one line in a notebook and end with a surveyor's fixed mark in the ground.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从笔记本上的一行字开始，落到测量员钉在地里的固定标记。

normal.en: One datum is a stone; data is the wall built from it.
normal.cn: 一个数据是一块石头，数据是一堵用石头砌成的墙。

normal.en: The word means given, because a fact is handed to you before you reason.
normal.cn: 这个词意为「被给出」，因为事实总在你推理之前就被递到手上。

normal.en: Keep the singular and you keep the habit of counting carefully.
normal.cn: 守住单数，就守住了仔细计数的习惯。

normal.en: Every measurement needs one point that refuses to move.
normal.cn: 每次测量都需要一个不肯移动的点。

normal.en: Datum is the word a careful engineer still writes in a report.
normal.cn: 严谨的工程师在报告里仍然会写 datum。

abstract.en: Picture a single number underlined twice in a lab book.
abstract.cn: 想象实验本上一个被划了两道线的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a brass pin set in concrete before any building starts.
abstract.cn: 想象动工之前，一枚铜钉被嵌进混凝土。

abstract.en: Picture one dot on a graph with nothing else drawn yet.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上只画了一个点，别的都还没有。

examples.en: One datum was enough to change their conclusion.
examples.cn: 一个数据就足以改变他们的结论。

examples.en: All heights were taken from the same datum.
examples.cn: 所有高度都从同一个基准点量起。

examples.en: Each datum in the table was checked twice.
examples.cn: 表格里的每一条数据都核对了两遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 datum 记成「得Ta」：得（dei）到一个答案，靠的就是这一条数据。

root: 拉丁语 datum 意为「被给出之物」，是 dare（给出）的过去分词中性形式，最初指论证前已被授予的起点；十七世纪进入英语测量术语，指固定基准点，十八世纪起成为实验与统计中单个事实或数值的名称。

sensesIntro.en: From one given fact, to the fixed point from which all measuring starts.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被给出的一条事实，到一切测量所依据的那个定点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one underlined number in a notebook of measurements.
core.cn: 核心意象：测量笔记本里一个画了线的数字。

branches.en: The first sense is the smallest unit of evidence.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是证据的最小单位。

branches.en: The second turns the unit into a point in space.
branches.cn: 第二个把这个单位变成空间中的一个点。

branches.en: Both senses need something given before anything can be built.
branches.cn: 两个义项都要先有「被给出的东西」，才能开始搭建。

branches.en: A surveyor's mark is itself one datum among many.
branches.cn: 测量员的标记本身也是众多数据中的一条。

branches.en: The word keeps asking where the figure came from.
branches.cn: 这个词始终在问：这个数字是从哪里来的。

intro.en: Datum is the singular trunk from which data, database, and databank all branch.
intro.cn: datum 是主干单数，data、database 与 databank 都从它分枝出去。

latinIntro.en: The Latin participle datum, given, is the source of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语分词 datum（被给出的）是整个词族的源头。

items.example: A single datum cannot prove the theory.
items.exampleCN: 一个数据无法证明这个理论。

items.example: The database holds ten years of records.
items.exampleCN: 这个数据库存着十年的记录。

items.example: The databank is open to researchers.

items.meaning: the fixed point of a survey
items.example: They set a datum point on the hill.
items.exampleCN: 他们在山上设了基准点。

items.meaning: the line drawn from that point
the surface used as a base

items.example: Each raw datum went into the file.
items.exampleCN: 每条原始数据都进了档案。

latinEntries.example: Dare is the verb behind datum.
latinEntries.exampleCN: dare 是 datum 背后的动词。

definition_zh: v. 使气馁；使胆怯；使沮丧
definition_en: to make someone feel frightened or discouraged about a task ahead
core_image: 一座高山挡在路口，行人的脚步在坡前慢了下来
scene: 再难的任务也吓不倒她。No task could daunt her.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：daunt 指使胆怯、使气馁；句意是任何任务都吓不倒她。

senses.title: Discourage
senses.definition: to make someone lose confidence before a task
senses.definitionCN: 使某人在任务面前失去信心
senses.example: The size of the job daunted him.
senses.exampleCN: 这项工作的规模让他气馁。
senses.why: A mountain standing across the road.
senses.whyCN: 一座横在路口的大山。

senses.title: Frighten
senses.definition: to make someone feel afraid of what lies ahead
senses.definitionCN: 使某人害怕前方的事物
senses.example: The storm did not daunt the sailors.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴没有让水手们胆怯。
senses.why: A small boat facing a tall wave.
senses.whyCN: 一只面对高浪的小船。

intro.en: Daunt comes from Old French danter, to tame, from Latin domitare, to subdue.
intro.cn: daunt 源自古法语 danter（驯服），再溯至拉丁语 domitare（制服）。

items.en: Domare meant to tame a wild animal.
items.cn: domare 意为驯服野兽。

items.en: Domitare was the repeated form, to keep taming.
items.cn: domitare 是反复形式，意为不断驯服。

items.en: Danter meant to tame or subdue.
items.cn: danter 意为驯服或制服。

items.en: Daunte entered English as to overcome.
items.cn: 十三世纪 daunte 以「制服」义进入英语。

items.en: Daunt shifted to discouraging a person.
items.cn: 十六世纪 daunt 转为使人沮丧。

items.en: Dauntless and daunting became common.
items.cn: 十九世纪 dauntless 与 daunting 变得常用。

note.en: The look-alike group swaps one letter; the near-meaning group names ways of losing heart.
note.cn: 形近组只换一个字母；近义组都是「让人泄气」的说法。

entries.definition: To spread paint or mud roughly.
To insult someone to provoke them.
To frighten someone into doing something.
To fill someone with worried surprise.
To stop someone by fear of the results.

normalIntro.en: Daunt sounds like aunt: an aunt whose strict look stops you.
normalIntro.cn: daunt 听起来像 aunt：一位严厉得让你止步的姑姑。

normal.en: An aunt can look very strict.
normal.cn: 姑姑可能看起来很严厉。

normal.en: A daunt is that stopping feeling.
normal.cn: daunt 就是那种让你止步的感觉。

normal.en: Latin domare means to tame.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 domare 意为驯服。

normal.en: To daunt is to tame the courage of someone.
normal.cn: daunt 就是驯掉某人的勇气。

normal.en: Dauntless means the courage stays wild.
normal.cn: dauntless 意为勇气依然未被驯服。

abstract.en: A mountain standing across the road.
abstract.cn: 一座横在路口的大山。

abstract.en: A small boat facing a tall wave.
abstract.cn: 一只面对高浪的小船。

abstract.en: A wild horse that refuses the rope.
abstract.cn: 一匹拒绝绳索的野马。

examples.en: The exam did not daunt the students.
examples.cn: 考试没有让学生们胆怯。

examples.en: It was a daunting climb, but she finished it.
examples.cn: 那是一次令人望而生畏的攀登，但她完成了。

examples.en: Nothing daunted, they started again.
examples.cn: 他们毫不气馁，重新开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「当特」——当面一座特别高的山；词源 domare（驯服），把勇气驯掉就是 daunt。

root: 拉丁 domare（驯服）→ domitare → 古法语 danter → 英语 daunt

sensesIntro.en: One taming: of courage and of confidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种驯服：驯掉勇气，也驯掉信心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mountain that slows a step before it starts
core.cn: 核心意象：一座让脚步在出发前就慢下来的山

branches.en: A mountain standing across the road.
branches.cn: 一座横在路口的大山。

branches.en: A small boat facing a tall wave.
branches.cn: 一只面对高浪的小船。

branches.en: A size that tames the will.
branches.cn: 一种驯服意志的体量。

branches.en: A wild horse that refuses the rope.
branches.cn: 一匹拒绝绳索的野马。

branches.en: Courage that stays untamed.
branches.cn: 依然未被驯服的勇气。

intro.en: Daunt carries the taming root dom-; -less and -ing build its two adjectives.
intro.cn: daunt 带着表示驯服的词根 dom-；-less 与 -ing 造出它的两个形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin domare means to tame and timere means to fear.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 domare 意为驯服，timere 意为害怕。

definition_zh: n. 恍惚；茫然 v. 使发懵；使眼花缭乱
definition_en: a confused state in which one cannot think clearly, or to stun someone into that state
core_image: 一盏强灯直照眼睛，世界忽然变成一片白噪
scene: 他撞到头后一直恍恍惚惚。He walked around in a daze after hitting his head.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：daze 指恍惚茫然的状态；句意是他撞到头后一直恍恍惚惚。

collocations.phrase: to come out of a daze

senses.title: Confused state
senses.definition: a state in which the mind cannot think clearly
senses.definitionCN: 头脑无法清晰思考的状态
senses.example: She sat in a daze for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 她恍惚地坐了一个小时。
senses.why: A room where every sound is far away.
senses.whyCN: 一个所有声音都很远的房间。

senses.title: Stun someone
senses.definition: to shock or blind someone into confusion
senses.definitionCN: 用震惊或强光使人陷入混乱
senses.example: The bright light dazed the driver.
senses.exampleCN: 强光晃得司机发懵。
senses.why: A white flash that empties the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 一道把眼睛掏空的白光。

intro.en: Daze comes from Old Norse dasi, a tired or stunned person.
intro.cn: daze 源自古诺斯语 dasi（疲惫或发懵的人）。

items.en: Dasi named a weary or stunned person.
items.cn: dasi 指疲惫或发懵的人。

items.en: Dasen meant to stun or exhaust.
items.cn: dasen 意为使发懵或使疲惫。

items.en: Daze appears as a verb of stunning.
items.cn: 十四世纪 daze 作为「使发懵」的动词出现。

items.en: Daze also became a noun of confusion.
items.cn: 十六世纪 daze 也成为表示茫然的名词。

items.en: Dazed became the common adjective.
items.cn: 十九世纪 dazed 成为常用形容词。

items.en: In a daze became a fixed everyday phrase.
items.cn: 二十世纪 in a daze 成为固定的日常短语。

note.en: The look-alike group swaps one letter; the near-meaning group names other stunned states.
note.cn: 形近组只换一个字母；近义组是其他发懵的状态。

entries.definition: To blind someone with bright light.
To sleep lightly for a short time.
A state of almost no feeling or thought.
A state of being totally confused.

normalIntro.en: Daze sounds like doze: awake, but the mind is asleep.
normalIntro.cn: daze 听起来像 doze：人醒着，脑子却睡着了。

normal.en: Doze means to sleep lightly.
normal.cn: doze 意为浅睡。

normal.en: Daze means the mind dozes while awake.
normal.cn: daze 意为醒着时脑子在打盹。

normal.en: A blow can daze a person.
normal.cn: 一击可以让人发懵。

normal.en: A bright light can daze the eyes.
normal.cn: 强光可以晃花眼睛。

normal.en: In a daze, time moves strangely.
normal.cn: 恍惚之中，时间走得很怪。

abstract.en: A room where every sound is far away.
abstract.cn: 一个所有声音都很远的房间。

abstract.en: A white flash that empties the eyes.
abstract.cn: 一道把眼睛掏空的白光。

abstract.en: A mind asleep behind open eyes.
abstract.cn: 一双睁着的眼睛后面睡着的脑子。

examples.en: He was in a daze after the news.
examples.cn: 听到消息后他一片茫然。

examples.en: The flash dazed everyone in the room.
examples.cn: 那道闪光让屋里所有人都发懵。

examples.en: She snapped out of her daze and stood up.
examples.cn: 她从恍惚中回过神，站了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「戴兹」——脑袋被戴上一罩子；与 doze（打盹）同韵，醒着却在梦游。

root: 古诺斯语 dasi（疲惫者）→ 中古英语 dasen（使发懵）→ daze

sensesIntro.en: One white flash: a state and a cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一道白光：一种状态，也是一个原因。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: open eyes with a sleeping mind behind them
core.cn: 核心意象：一双睁着的眼睛后面睡着的脑子

branches.en: A room where every sound is far away.
branches.cn: 一个所有声音都很远的房间。

branches.en: A white flash that empties the eyes.
branches.cn: 一道把眼睛掏空的白光。

branches.en: A flash that leaves a blank.
branches.cn: 一道留下空白的闪光。

branches.en: A mind asleep behind open eyes.
branches.cn: 一双睁着的眼睛后面睡着的脑子。

branches.en: A blow that stops the clock.
branches.cn: 一下让时钟停摆的撞击。

intro.en: Daze is a short Norse borrowing; -ed turns it into an adjective.
intro.cn: daze 是一个短的诺斯语借词；-ed 把它变成形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin stupere means to be stunned and lux means light.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stupere 意为发懵，lux 意为光。

definition_zh: v. 使眼花缭乱；使赞叹 n. 耀眼的光；令人赞叹之物
definition_en: to blind someone with bright light or amaze them with brilliance, or the bright light itself
core_image: 舞台灯一齐打过来，观众眼里只剩一片跳动的金星
scene: 她的表演让观众惊叹不已。Her performance dazzled the audience.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：dazzle 指令人赞叹；句意是她的表演让观众惊叹不已。

pos.zh: 耀眼的光；令人赞叹之物

collocations.phrase: to be dazzled by the glare

senses.title: Blind with light
senses.definition: to make someone unable to see because of bright light
senses.definitionCN: 因强光使人暂时看不见
senses.example: The headlights dazzled the cyclist.
senses.exampleCN: 车灯晃得骑车人睁不开眼。
senses.why: A white starburst in the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 眼里一片白色的星芒。

senses.title: Amaze with skill
senses.definition: to impress someone greatly with skill or beauty
senses.definitionCN: 以技艺或美貌使人极为倾倒
senses.example: She dazzled the judges with her speed.
senses.exampleCN: 她以速度征服了评委。
senses.why: A stage where every eye follows one person.
senses.whyCN: 一个所有目光追着一个人的舞台。

senses.title: Bright display
senses.definition: a brilliant show of light or colour
senses.definitionCN: 一片夺目的光或色彩
senses.example: The dazzle of the city at night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜晚城市的炫目光华。
senses.why: A river of moving lights.
senses.whyCN: 一条流动的光河。

intro.en: Dazzle is daze plus the repeated-action ending -le.
intro.cn: dazzle 由 daze 加表示反复动作的词尾 -le 构成。

items.en: Dasi named a stunned person.
items.cn: dasi 指发懵的人。

items.en: Dasen meant to stun with a blow.
items.cn: dasen 意为一击使人发懵。

items.en: Dasel added the repeated ending -el.
items.cn: 十五世纪 dasel 加上反复词尾 -el。

items.en: Dazzle came to mean blinding with light.
items.cn: 十六世纪 dazzle 转为「以强光晃眼」。

items.en: Dazzle gained the sense of amazing skill.
items.cn: 十八世纪 dazzle 获得「技艺惊人」的意思。

items.en: Dazzle paint hid ships by confusing the eye.
items.cn: 二十世纪炫目迷彩靠扰乱视线来隐藏船只。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the daz- shape; the near-meaning group names kinds of brightness.
note.cn: 形近组共享 daz- 的形状；近义组是各种「亮」。

entries.definition: A cover for the mouth of an animal.
To give out or reflect light.
To shine with small bright flashes.

normalIntro.en: Dazzle is daze plus -le: light that keeps stunning you.
normalIntro.cn: dazzle 就是 daze 加 -le：不断把你晃懵的光。

normal.en: Daze means to stun.
normal.cn: daze 意为使发懵。

normal.en: The ending -le means again and again.
normal.cn: -le 表示反复发生。

normal.en: Dazzle is light stunning you repeatedly.
normal.cn: dazzle 就是光反复晃你。

normal.en: A dazzle can also be pure skill.
normal.cn: dazzle 也可以是纯粹的技艺。

normal.en: Dazzling paint confused the eye at sea.
normal.cn: 炫目迷彩在海上扰乱视线。

abstract.en: A white starburst in the eyes.
abstract.cn: 眼里一片白色的星芒。

abstract.en: A stage where every eye follows one person.
abstract.cn: 一个所有目光追着一个人的舞台。

abstract.en: A river of moving lights.
abstract.cn: 一条流动的光河。

examples.en: The sun dazzled us as we left the tunnel.
examples.cn: 出隧道时阳光晃得我们睁不开眼。

examples.en: Her dazzling smile won the whole room.
examples.cn: 她耀眼的笑容征服了全场。

examples.en: The dazzle of the fireworks faded slowly.
examples.cn: 烟火的炫光慢慢褪去。

dict_mnemonic.text: daze（发懵）+ -le（反复）＝反复把你晃懵；谐音「大杂亮」——一大片杂乱的强光。

root: 古诺斯语 dasi → 中古英语 dasen（使发懵）+ -le（反复）→ dazzle

sensesIntro.en: One bright shock: eyes, skill and city light.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一次亮的冲击：眼睛、技艺与城市灯火。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a starburst of light that takes the eyes
core.cn: 核心意象：一团夺走视线的星芒强光

branches.en: A white starburst in the eyes.
branches.cn: 眼里一片白色的星芒。

branches.en: A stage where every eye follows one person.
branches.cn: 一个所有目光追着一个人的舞台。

branches.en: A river of moving lights.
branches.cn: 一条流动的光河。

branches.en: Light and skill both take the eyes.
branches.cn: 光与技艺都夺走目光。

branches.en: A show that refuses to be ignored.
branches.cn: 一场无法被忽视的展示。

intro.en: Dazzle is daze plus -le; -ing turns it into the adjective dazzling.
intro.cn: dazzle 由 daze 加 -le 构成；-ing 把它变成形容词 dazzling。

latinIntro.en: Latin lux means light and micare means to flash.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lux 意为光，micare 意为闪烁。

definition_en: no longer alive, or no longer working
core_image: 一只停在窗台上、再也不动的鸟
scene: 那只鸟落在窗台上，再也没动过。The old tree in the yard is dead.
sceneCN: 这里 dead 指「死的」（第 1 个义项：不再有生命的）；句意是院子里的老树已经死了。

senses.title: No longer alive
senses.definition: having stopped living and unable to move or grow
senses.definitionCN: 已经停止生命、不能动也不再生长的
senses.example: The old tree in the yard is dead.
senses.exampleCN: 院子里的老树已经死了。
senses.why: The word marks a line that cannot be crossed back.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出一条无法回头跨过的界线。

senses.title: No longer working
senses.definition: having stopped working, as a battery or a phone
senses.definitionCN: 像电池或手机那样停止工作
senses.example: The phone went dead during the call.
senses.exampleCN: 电话打着打着就没电了。
senses.why: A machine that stops looks exactly like a body that stops.
senses.whyCN: 停下的机器，看起来和停下的身体一模一样。

senses.title: Completely, to the limit
senses.definition: used to mean totally or exactly, as in dead tired
senses.definitionCN: 表示彻底或正好，如累到极点
senses.example: I was dead tired after the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班之后我累得不行。
senses.why: Something that is dead has gone as far as it can go.
senses.whyCN: 已经死去的东西，是走到了尽头。

intro.en: Dead is an Old English adjective, dēad, with the same shape across the Germanic languages.
intro.cn: dead 是古英语形容词 dēad，在整个日耳曼语族里形状相同。

items.en: A root meaning to die lies behind the Germanic forms.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的这些形式背后，有一个意为「死去」的词根。

items.en: Dēad described a body from which life had gone.
items.cn: dēad 形容生命已经离去的身体。

items.en: Norse dauðr kept the same sense in the north.
items.cn: 诺尔斯语 dauðr 在北方保留了同样的意思。

items.en: Dead began to be used for tools and for languages out of use.
items.cn: dead 开始用于工具和不再使用的语言。

items.en: The adverb use, as in dead tired, fixed the idea of totalness.
items.cn: 副词用法如 dead tired，把「彻底」的意思固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the d- opening and short vowel, and the meaning group moves from bodies to machines.
note.cn: 形近组共享 d 开头与短元音，近义组则从身体走到机器。

entries.definition: to be brave enough to do something
a formal word for a person who has died
no longer existing as a species
entries.definitionCN: 作为一个物种已不复存在的

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a bird that does not move and end with a phone that gives no answer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只不再动的鸟开始，落到一部不再应答的手机。

normal.en: Dead is a line, not a degree; there is no more or less.
normal.cn: 死是一条界线，不是程度，没有多一点少一点。

normal.en: A still bird and a still machine look the same from far away.
normal.cn: 远处看，静止的鸟和静止的机器没有分别。

normal.en: The word once meant only bodies; now it means batteries too.
normal.cn: 这个词从前只指身体，现在也指电池。

normal.en: Dead tired means tired all the way down.
normal.cn: dead tired 是指累到了最底下。

normal.en: A dead language is one nobody wakes up speaking.
normal.cn: 死语言，就是没人一早醒来会说的语言。

abstract.en: Picture a garden chair with no one in it.
abstract.cn: 想象院子里一把没人坐的椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a screen that stays black after a click.
abstract.cn: 想象点了之后依然黑着的屏幕。

abstract.en: Picture a branch that breaks instead of bending.
abstract.cn: 想象一根不弯、直接断掉的树枝。

examples.en: The old tree in the yard is dead.
examples.cn: 院子里的老树已经死了。

examples.en: The phone went dead during the call.
examples.cn: 电话打着打着就没电了。

examples.en: We stopped at a dead end and turned back.
examples.cn: 我们在死胡同前停下，掉头回去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dead 记成「呆的」：呆着一动不动，就是没有生气了。

root: 源自古英语 dēad，与古诺尔斯语 dauðr 等同源，更早可上溯到印欧语中表示「死去」的词根；十四世纪起从身体扩展到工具与语言，副词用法又引申出「彻底、正好」的意思。

sensesIntro.en: From a body without life, to a machine without power, to a word meaning completely.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没有生命的身体，到没有电的机器，再到表示彻底的那个词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bird on a sill that never moves again.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗台上一只再不动的鸟。

branches.en: The first sense is the biological line that cannot be crossed back.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那条无法回头跨过的生理界线。

branches.en: The second lends that stillness to anything that has stopped.
branches.cn: 第二个把这种静止借给一切停下来的东西。

branches.en: The third turns the end point into a measure of completeness.
branches.cn: 第三个把终点变成一种彻底的程度。

branches.en: A dead battery and a dead bird share only the stillness.
branches.cn: 没电的电池和死去的鸟，只共享那份静止。

branches.en: Going dead and going all the way are the same direction.
branches.cn: 「停死」和「走到底」是同一个方向。

intro.en: Dead is a small but productive family, with nouns and verbs built on the idea of stopped life.
intro.cn: dead 这一族不大却能产词，名词和动词都建在「生命停住」这个意思上。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved; dead is a native Germanic adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词不涉及拉丁词根，dead 是本族日耳曼形容词。

items.meaning: to make less strong or less felt
the state of being without life
items.example: A strange deadness filled the room.
items.exampleCN: 屋里充满一种奇怪的死寂。

items.meaning: a road or plan with no way on
items.example: The job was a dead end.

definition_en: the latest time by which something must be finished
core_image: 墙上的钟快指到午夜，桌上还堆着没写完的稿子
scene: 编辑在日历上圈出周五，说那天必须交稿。The deadline is Friday at noon.
sceneCN: 这里 deadline 指「截止期限」（第 1 个义项：必须完成某事的最晚时间）；句意是截止时间是周五中午。

senses.title: The last moment allowed
senses.definition: the fixed time after which work is no longer accepted
senses.definitionCN: 过了这个时间，工作就不再被接受
senses.example: The deadline is Friday at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 截止时间是周五中午。
senses.why: A line drawn across time works like a line drawn on the ground.
senses.whyCN: 在时间上画的一条线，和在地上画的一条线一样管用。

senses.title: A line one must not cross
senses.definition: the original sense: a boundary in a prison camp that guards would shoot across
senses.definitionCN: 最初的义项：战俘营里一道越过去就会被开枪射击的界线
senses.example: The old prison deadline was marked with white stones.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧战俘营的界线是用白石标出的。
senses.why: The word began as a line you crossed only once, and time borrowed its force.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是一条只能越一次的线，时间借走了它的力量。

intro.en: Deadline first named a real line on the ground in an American prison camp during the civil war.
intro.cn: deadline 最初指美国内战时期战俘营地上一条真实的界线。

items.en: A deadline was a line past which prisoners would be shot.
items.cn: deadline 指战俘越过就会被射杀的界线。

items.en: Printers used the word for a line of type beyond the page.
items.cn: 印刷工用它指超出页面的一道字行。

items.en: Newspapers used deadline for the hour a story had to be in.
items.cn: 报社用它指稿件必须交到的钟点。

items.en: The word spread from newsrooms into every kind of work.
items.cn: 这个词从新闻编辑室扩散到各行各业。

items.en: A deadline is now any moment that ends the time allowed.
items.cn: 如今 deadline 指任何结束允许时间的时刻。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dead- or -line shape, and the meaning group names other ends of time.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dead- 或 -line 的词形，近义组则列出时间的其他终点。

entries.definitionCN: 不再活着或不再运转的

entries.definition: a state where neither side can move
entries.definitionCN: 双方都无法前进的僵局

entries.definition: the point at which something stops being allowed
entries.definitionCN: 某事不再被允许的那个点

entries.definition: the greatest amount or point permitted
entries.definitionCN: 被允许的最大量或最远点

entries.definition: the day on which something must be handed in
entries.definitionCN: 必须交上某物的那一天

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line on prison ground and end with a clock that refuses to wait.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从战俘营地上的一条线开始，落到一只不肯等人的钟。

normal.en: A deadline is a wall built out of minutes.
normal.cn: 截止期，是用分钟砌起来的一堵墙。

normal.en: The word once meant a line you could not walk past.
normal.cn: 这个词从前指一条不能走过去的线。

normal.en: Work stretches until a deadline gives it a shape.
normal.cn: 工作一直拖着，直到截止期给它一个形状。

normal.en: A missed deadline is louder than a late excuse.
normal.cn: 错过的截止期，比迟到的解释更响。

normal.en: The clock does not move faster; only the room does.
normal.cn: 钟没有走快，是屋里的人变快了。

abstract.en: Picture a clock on a wall and a page still blank.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一只钟，桌上还是一张白纸。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a folder across a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把文件夹推过柜台。

abstract.en: Picture white stones laid in a straight line on bare ground.
abstract.cn: 想象空地上用白石摆出的一条直线。

examples.en: The deadline is Friday at noon.
examples.cn: 截止时间是周五中午。

examples.en: They worked all night to meet the deadline.
examples.cn: 为了赶上截止期，他们干了一整夜。

examples.en: The editor agreed to extend the deadline by a week.
examples.cn: 编辑同意把截止期延长一周。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deadline 记成「死线」：dead 是死，line 是线，一条过了就完了的线，就是截止期。

root: 由 dead（死的）与 line（线）复合而成，十九世纪六十年代美国战俘营里指越界即被射杀的界线；印刷业与报社先后借用，二十世纪起泛指一切必须完成工作的最后时刻。

sensesIntro.en: From a line on the ground you must not cross, to a line on the clock you must not pass.
sensesIntro.cn: 从地上不能越过的线，到钟上不能越过的线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn across time with a clock behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：横在时间上的一条线，身后是一只钟。

branches.en: The first sense is the modern one: the last accepted moment.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是现代义：最后被接受的那一刻。

branches.en: The second is the literal line that gave the word its force.
branches.cn: 第二个是给这个词以力量的那条真实的线。

branches.en: Both senses share one rule: past this point, there is no return.
branches.cn: 两个义项共用一条规矩：过了这点，就回不去了。

branches.en: The prison line became a metaphor the moment offices needed one.
branches.cn: 办公室一需要比喻，战俘营的那条线就变成了比喻。

branches.en: A deadline is frightening because it remembers being deadly.
branches.cn: 截止期之所以吓人，是因为它记得自己曾经致命。

intro.en: Deadline is a compound, so its family is built by pairing it with the verbs and nouns of work.
intro.cn: deadline 是复合词，它的一族靠与工作相关的动词和名词搭配而成。

latinIntro.en: The two halves are native English: dead from Old English dēad, line from Latin linea through French.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都算英语本族：dead 出自古英语 dēad，line 则经法语来自拉丁语 linea。

items.meaning: to fail to finish in time
items.example: He missed the deadline by a day.

items.meaning: a deadline that leaves little time
items.example: She works well under a tight deadline.
items.exampleCN: 期限紧迫时她反而干得好。

items.meaning: the stress caused by a deadline
items.example: Deadline pressure kept him at his desk.
items.exampleCN: 截止期的压力把他按在桌前。

definition_zh: n. 僵局；僵持；（计算机）死锁
definition_en: a situation in which no progress is possible because opposing sides refuse to move
core_image: 两把钥匙同时插进同一把锁，谁也转不动
scene: 谈判陷入僵局。The talks ended in a deadlock.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：deadlock 指双方都不让步的僵局；句意是谈判以僵局告终。

senses.title: No progress
senses.definition: a standstill caused by two sides refusing to give way
senses.definitionCN: 双方都不让步而造成的停滞
senses.example: The strike produced a deadlock.
senses.exampleCN: 罢工造成了僵局。
senses.why: Two keys turning against each other in one lock.
senses.whyCN: 两把钥匙在同一把锁里互相较劲。

senses.title: Computing wait
senses.definition: a state where processes each wait for the other to release a resource
senses.definitionCN: 进程互相等待对方释放资源的状态
senses.example: The program froze in a deadlock.
senses.exampleCN: 程序因死锁而卡住。
senses.why: Two hands each holding the other pen.
senses.whyCN: 两只手各握着对方的笔。

intro.en: Deadlock is dead plus lock: a lock that will not turn.
intro.cn: deadlock 由 dead 加 lock 构成：一把转不动的锁。

items.en: Dead meant without life or motion.
items.cn: dead 意为没有生命或不动。

items.en: Loc meant a bolt or fastening.
items.cn: loc 意为门闩或扣件。

items.en: Deadlock named a lock that would not open.
items.cn: 十八世纪 deadlock 指打不开的锁。

items.en: Deadlock became a word for a stuck dispute.
items.cn: 十九世纪 deadlock 成为争执僵持的用词。

items.en: Deadlock described hung parliaments and talks.
items.cn: 二十世纪 deadlock 用来描述悬峙议会与谈判。

items.en: Deadlock names a resource wait in software.
items.cn: 二十一世纪 deadlock 指软件中的资源互等。

note.en: The look-alike group shares dead-; the near-meaning group names other standstills.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dead-；近义组是其他停滞状态。

entries.definition: The latest time for finishing something.
A journey made without passengers or cargo.
A lock that hangs from a hasp.
A position where neither side can move.
A traffic jam where nothing can move.

normalIntro.en: Deadlock is dead plus lock: a lock with no life in it.
normalIntro.cn: deadlock 就是 dead 加 lock：一把没有活气的锁。

normal.en: Dead means not moving.
normal.cn: dead 意为不动。

normal.en: A lock holds a door shut.
normal.cn: 锁把门锁住。

normal.en: A deadlock is a lock that will not turn.
normal.cn: deadlock 就是转不动的锁。

normal.en: Two sides hold each other still.
normal.cn: 双方把彼此按住不动。

normal.en: A third key can break the deadlock.
normal.cn: 第三把钥匙能打破僵局。

abstract.en: Two keys turning against each other in one lock.
abstract.cn: 两把钥匙在同一把锁里互相较劲。

abstract.en: Two hands each holding the other pen.
abstract.cn: 两只手各握着对方的笔。

abstract.en: A door with no key that fits.
abstract.cn: 一扇没有合适钥匙的门。

examples.en: The deadlock lasted three weeks.
examples.cn: 僵局持续了三个星期。

examples.en: A small compromise broke the deadlock.
examples.cn: 一个小小的妥协打破了僵局。

examples.en: The two processes deadlocked over one file.
examples.cn: 两个进程为同一个文件陷入死锁。

dict_mnemonic.text: dead（死的）+ lock（锁）＝死锁；两把钥匙互相较劲，谁也转不动。

root: 古英语 dead（不动）+ loc（门闩）→ 十八世纪 deadlock（打不开的锁）→ 僵局

sensesIntro.en: One stuck lock: in talks and in software.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一把卡住的锁：在谈判里，也在软件里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two keys jammed in one lock
core.cn: 核心意象：两把钥匙卡在同一把锁里

branches.en: Two keys turning against each other in one lock.
branches.cn: 两把钥匙在同一把锁里互相较劲。

branches.en: Two hands each holding the other pen.
branches.cn: 两只手各握着对方的笔。

branches.en: Each side waits for the other to move.
branches.cn: 双方都等对方先动。

branches.en: A door with no key that fits.
branches.cn: 一扇没有合适钥匙的门。

branches.en: A circle of waiting with no end.
branches.cn: 一圈没有尽头的等待。

intro.en: Deadlock is dead plus lock; its neighbours share stop and fastening roots.
intro.cn: deadlock 由 dead 加 lock 构成；相邻词共享「停」与「扣紧」的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin claudere means to close and stare means to stand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 claudere 意为关闭，stare 意为站立。

definition_zh: adj. 致命的；极度的 adv. 非常；极度地
definition_en: causing or able to cause death; also used as an intensifier meaning extremely
core_image: 一支尖端发黑的小箭，与一句「极其认真」同样不容轻视
scene: 这种蛇的毒液是致命的。The snake venom is deadly.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：deadly 指致命的；句意是这种蛇的毒液能致死。

senses.title: Causing death
senses.definition: able to cause death
senses.definitionCN: 能够致死的
senses.example: The bite of this spider can be deadly.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蜘蛛的咬伤可能致命。
senses.why: A small arrow with a dark tip.
senses.whyCN: 一支尖端发黑的小箭。

senses.title: Extreme degree
senses.definition: used to stress how complete something is
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调某事的彻底程度
senses.example: He was deadly serious about the promise.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这个承诺极其认真。
senses.why: A face with no smile left in it.
senses.whyCN: 一张再无笑意的脸。

senses.title: Intensifier
senses.definition: very or extremely, placed before an adjective
senses.definitionCN: 非常、极度地，用在形容词前
senses.example: The test was deadly dull.
senses.exampleCN: 那次考试枯燥得要命。
senses.why: A clock whose hands barely move.
senses.whyCN: 一只指针几乎不动的钟。

intro.en: Deadly is dead plus -ly, an adjective ending meaning like or causing.
intro.cn: deadly 由 dead 加形容词词尾 -ly 构成，意为「像…的」或「致…的」。

items.en: Dead meant without life.
items.cn: dead 意为没有生命。

items.en: The ending -lic meant having the nature of.
items.cn: 词尾 -lic 意为「具有…性质」。

items.en: Deadlic meant causing death.
items.cn: deadlic 意为致死的。

items.en: Deadly kept the fatal sense.
items.cn: 十三世纪 deadly 保留致命义。

items.en: Deadly became an intensifier in speech.
items.cn: 十六世纪 deadly 在口语中成为强调词。

items.en: Deadly dull and deadly serious became fixed uses.
items.cn: 二十世纪 deadly dull 与 deadly serious 成为固定用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares dead-; the near-meaning group names other fatal words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dead-；近义组是其他表示「致死」的词。

normalIntro.en: Deadly is dead plus -ly: like death, then like nothing else.
normalIntro.cn: deadly 就是 dead 加 -ly：像死亡一样，再引申为「无比」。

normal.en: Dead means without life.
normal.cn: dead 意为没有生命。

normal.en: The ending -ly can build adjectives.
normal.cn: -ly 也能构成形容词。

normal.en: Deadly first means causing death.
normal.cn: deadly 最初意为致死。

normal.en: Then it means extreme, as total as death.
normal.cn: 接着它表示极端，像死亡一样彻底。

normal.en: Deadly dull means dull beyond bearing.
normal.cn: deadly dull 意为枯燥到难以忍受。

abstract.en: A small arrow with a dark tip.
abstract.cn: 一支尖端发黑的小箭。

abstract.en: A face with no smile left in it.
abstract.cn: 一张再无笑意的脸。

abstract.en: A clock whose hands barely move.
abstract.cn: 一只指针几乎不动的钟。

examples.en: The two countries were deadly enemies.
examples.cn: 那两个国家是死敌。

examples.en: She is deadly accurate with a rifle.
examples.cn: 她用步枪极其精准。

examples.en: The lecture was deadly boring.
examples.cn: 那场讲座无聊透顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: dead（死）+ -ly（形容词尾）＝像死一样；从「致命」引申到「极度」，deadly serious 就是认真到极点。

root: 古英语 dead（死）+ -lic（具有…性质）→ deadlic → deadly

sensesIntro.en: One deathly degree: fatal, total and very.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种「死一般的程度」：致命、彻底与非常。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark-tipped arrow that ends everything
core.cn: 核心意象：一支终结一切的黑色箭头

branches.en: A small arrow with a dark tip.
branches.cn: 一支尖端发黑的小箭。

branches.en: A face with no smile left in it.
branches.cn: 一张再无笑意的脸。

branches.en: A clock whose hands barely move.
branches.cn: 一只指针几乎不动的钟。

branches.en: Death used as a measure of degree.
branches.cn: 用死亡来度量程度。

branches.en: A word that pushes to the end.
branches.cn: 一个把程度推到尽头的词。

intro.en: Deadly is dead plus -ly; -er and -est build its comparisons.
intro.cn: deadly 由 dead 加 -ly 构成；-er 与 -est 造出它的比较级。

latinIntro.en: Latin mors means death and letum means violent death.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mors 意为死亡，letum 意为暴死。

definition_en: unable to hear, or refusing to listen
core_image: 一个人把手掌贴在耳后，仍然听不见
scene: 老人把手拢在耳后，还是听不清孙子的声音。The old man has been deaf since childhood.
sceneCN: 这里 deaf 指「聋的」（第 1 个义项：听不见声音的）；句意是这位老人从小就聋。

senses.title: Unable to hear
senses.definition: having little or no ability to hear sounds
senses.definitionCN: 几乎没有或完全没有听见声音的能力
senses.example: The old man has been deaf since childhood.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老人从小就聋。
senses.why: The word describes the ear, not the sound; the sound is still there.
senses.whyCN: 这个词说的是耳朵，不是声音；声音一直都在。

senses.title: Refusing to listen
senses.definition: choosing not to pay attention to advice or appeals
senses.definitionCN: 选择不去理会劝告或请求
senses.example: He was deaf to every warning we gave.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的每一次警告他都听不进去。
senses.why: We borrow the ear's condition to describe the will's refusal.
senses.whyCN: 我们借耳朵的状况，来形容意志的拒绝。

intro.en: Deaf is an Old English adjective, dēaf, with close relatives in Dutch and German.
intro.cn: deaf 是古英语形容词 dēaf，在荷兰语和德语里都有近亲。

items.en: A root suggesting dullness of sense lies behind the word.
items.cn: 这个词背后有一个表示感官迟钝的词根。

items.en: Dēaf meant unable to hear, and also dull or empty.
items.cn: dēaf 既指听不见，也指迟钝或空。

items.en: Norse daufr kept the same sense of not hearing.
items.cn: 诺尔斯语 daufr 保留了听不见的意思。

items.en: The figurative sense, deaf to advice, became common.
items.cn: deaf to advice 这类比喻用法变得常见。

items.en: Deaf now names both a condition and a refusal.
items.cn: 如今 deaf 既指一种状况，也指一种拒绝。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short e and final consonant, and the meaning group names ways of not responding.
note.cn: 形近组共享短元音 e 和词尾辅音，近义组则列出不回应的方式。

entries.definition: to give out cards or to handle a matter
not reacting to words or actions
entries.definitionCN: 对言语或行动没有反应的

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a hand cupped behind an ear and end with a warning that nobody answers.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拢在耳后的那只手开始，落到一句没人回应的警告。

normal.en: Deaf describes the ear; the world still speaks.
normal.cn: deaf 说的是耳朵，世界仍在说话。

normal.en: A deaf ear and a closed mind use the same word.
normal.cn: 聋的耳朵和关上的心，用的是同一个词。

normal.en: The word once also meant dull, as if the senses had gone quiet.
normal.cn: 这个词从前也指迟钝，仿佛感官安静了下来。

normal.en: Silence in a deaf room is not empty; it is full.
normal.cn: 聋人房里的安静并不空，它是满的。

normal.en: Turn a deaf ear and you choose to lose a warning.
normal.cn: 置若罔闻，就是选择丢掉一次警告。

abstract.en: Picture a hand cupped behind an ear in a crowded room.
abstract.cn: 想象拥挤的屋里，一只手拢在耳后。

abstract.en: Picture a mouth moving and no sound arriving.
abstract.cn: 想象一张嘴在动，声音却没有到达。

abstract.en: Picture eyes doing all the work the ears once did.
abstract.cn: 想象眼睛在做耳朵从前做的所有事。

examples.en: The old man has been deaf since childhood.
examples.cn: 这位老人从小就聋。

examples.en: She is deaf in one ear after the accident.
examples.cn: 事故之后她一只耳朵聋了。

examples.en: He turned a deaf ear to their advice.
examples.cn: 他对他们的劝告置若罔闻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deaf 记成「得夫」：耳朵听不见，只能靠眼睛「得」到信息，就像少了半边天。

root: 源自古英语 dēaf（听不见、迟钝），与荷兰语 doof、德语 taub 同源，更早可上溯到一个表示感官迟钝的印欧词根；中古英语起引申出「不愿听」的比喻义。

sensesIntro.en: From an ear that cannot catch sound, to a will that will not catch advice.
sensesIntro.cn: 从接不住声音的耳朵，到接不住劝告的意志。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand cupped behind an ear that still hears nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手拢在耳后，仍什么也听不见。

branches.en: The first sense is a physical limit of the ear.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是耳朵的生理限制。

branches.en: The second is a chosen limit of attention.
branches.cn: 第二个是主动选择的注意力限制。

branches.en: Both describe a door that does not open when someone knocks.
branches.cn: 两者都形容一扇有人敲却不开的门。

branches.en: The metaphor works because the condition is familiar.
branches.cn: 这个比喻成立，是因为那种状况人人熟悉。

branches.en: One is not a choice; the other is nothing but choice.
branches.cn: 一个是无从选择，一个纯粹是选择。

intro.en: Deaf has a small family of verbs, adjectives, and fixed phrases, all built on not hearing.
intro.cn: deaf 有一小族动词、形容词和固定短语，全都建立在「听不见」上。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here; deaf is a native Germanic adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，deaf 是本族日耳曼形容词。

items.example: The explosion deafened him for a day.

items.meaning: so loud it blocks all other sound

items.example: Deafness did not stop her work.
items.exampleCN: 失聪没有让她停下工作。

items.meaning: an old name for a hearing aid
items.example: He wore a deaf aid in one ear.
items.exampleCN: 他一只耳朵戴着助听器。

items.example: They were deaf to our appeals.
items.exampleCN: 他们对我们的请求充耳不闻。

items.example: She turned a deaf ear to the rumours.
